contexts.text: The first state is that which precedes, both that from infancy, and also that immediately before regeneration; and is called vacuity, emptiness, and thick darkness.

The earth was vacuity and emptiness ()... Man before regeneration is called the earth void and empty, and also ground in which nothing of good and truth has been inseminated: void, where there is nothing of good; and empty, where there is nothing of truth... which man is described in Jeremiah... I saw the earth, and lo, it was vacuity and emptiness ().
Then all things which are worthless are dissipated of themselves.
Worthless scientifics which he imbibes in childhood...
The city of emptiness which shall be broken () = the human mind which is deprived of truth.
Vain and empty things, as are those of the glory of the world and of self...
The desolation and vastation of truth is signified by the line of emptiness, and the perpendicular of wasteness (). (See Empty at AC 4744.)
Because they have a completely void and empty idea about the Divine...

In the Word there are double expressions, which appear to be repetitions... as vacuity and emptiness... These appear to be synonyms, but are not so; for... vacuity... is predicated of good, and in the opposite sense of evil; but... emptiness... of truth, and in the opposite of falsity.
The inanity of the ideas...
(They suppose) that I am like some empty thing.
He calls this an emptiness of idea.

They first appeared to me as if they were something completely inane; (for) when Spirits cherish the idea that they are a kind of general, atmospheric something, wandering about in the universe, they appear as a general inane something; in this instance as a most inane something, with scarcely any perception that they are Spirits. The reason was, that when (the Most Ancient) Church declined, they believed that their spirit or life after death would be of this character.
Void and empty () = that in the Church there was no good and truth.
He hath not created it empty () = that it is not devoid of the truth and good in which are those who have been reformed. The lack of them is emptiness.
That before there was no Church, because men were devoid of good and truth, is signified by the earth was void and empty ().
That the doctrine of falsity will be destroyed, is signified by the city of emptiness shall be broken; city = doctrine; and emptiness, falsity.
That the latter will be deprived, is signified by God hath sent the rich empty away ().

Wind and emptiness () = falsities of evil and evils of falsity; wind, the falsities of evil; and emptiness, the evils of falsity; for where there is what is empty and void, that is, what is devoid of good and truth, there is evil and falsity.
Wind and emptiness are predicated in the Word of falsities from proprium.
The city of emptiness = doctrine in which there is no truth, but falsity.
Egypt which is vanity and emptiness () = both the Sensuous and the Natural, which, regarded in themselves, are devoid of good and devoid of truths.
That in this faith there is no religion, but that it is emptiness and vacuity. Explained.
The wind which shall feed the shepherds () = the emptiness and vacuity of doctrine.
Hence it is evident that Babylon at its end is a Church void and empty of all good of love to God, and of all good of love towards the neighbour, and consequently of all truth...
The earth being called waste and empty () = that there was no longer any good of life or truth of doctrine with its inhabitants. Illustrated.
